note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Tonga: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: An individual or sole trader pays nothing on the first TOP 12,000 a year of gross income, 10% to 30,000, 15% to 50,000, 20% to 70,000 and 25% above, the Ministry of Revenue and Customs's "New Tax Rate" from July 2021, with no deductions for an employee; no later table is printed.
figures.applies: From 1 July 2021; read 2026-11-03 on the Ministry's own page, which prints no later table.

sources.said: The tax-free income level will be raised from the first $10,000 to the first $12,000 pa'anga earned in the new financial year, with further adjustments in tax thresholds easing higher income tax levels.

The current 10% income tax will be applied on income between $12,000 and $30,000 per annum. For earnings between $30,001 and $50,000, the rate will be reduced from 20% to 15%. Earnings between $50,0001 and $70,000 are subject to a $20% tax rate. Earnings over $70,001 are subject to a 25% tax rate.
Income tax cuts for individuals and sole traders from July 1 means all income taxpayers in Tonga will pay less.

New Tax Rate - July 2021 Gross Income Tax Rate $0 - $12,000 Nil $12,001 - $30,000 10% $30,001- $50,000 15% $50,001-$70,000 20% $70,001 and over 25% No Deduction Allowed Employees have no allowable deductions.

figures.finding: The employer withholds PAYE from an employee's gross pay at the tax rates of the table and pays it with a monthly return within 28 days after the month; the year's reconciliation is due on 31 August, and an individual in business files a return by 31 October.

value.paye: by the table on gross employment income
value.remit: within 28 days after the end of each month

figures.finding: A payer withholds 10% of the gross from a non-resident's fee for independent services (a visiting performer's, director's or producer's), and 15% from a royalty; the non-resident's liability is satisfied to the extent the tax is withheld, and the payer pays it within 28 days after the month.

value.final: yes: the non-resident's liability is satisfied to the extent the tax is withheld
value.remit: within 28 days after the end of the month

sources.said: The income tax imposed shall be 10% of the gross amount paid to a non-resident person rendering independent services.

a non-resident person’s liability for tax is satisfied to the extent that the tax payable is withheld by the payer from the amount paid to the non-resident person. The income tax imposed shall be: 5% of the gross amount of the insurance premium 15% of the gross amount of the interest, royalty, dividend, or technical services fee

figures.finding: A private-sector employee pays 5% of gross pay to the National Retirement Benefits Fund, deducted by the employer, and the employer at least 7.5% (of gross on the Fund's home page, of basic salary on its services page), monthly.
figures.applies: Members of the Fund (the private sector, from 1 July 2012); read 2026-11-03.

sources.said: Member Contribution Account (MC, 5% of gross) – mandated contribution deducted from members weekly/fortnightly/monthly or annual salary … Employer Contribution Account (EC, 7.5% of gross)
Employees must contribute 5% of his Montly Salary Employer must contribute minimum 7.5% based on employee basic salary

figures.finding: Consumption tax is 15% on most goods and services (since 1 April 2005); registration is compulsory once taxable supplies reach TOP 100,000 in twelve months.
figures.applies: Read 2026-11-03. The Ministry registers at TOP 100,000 or more; the game charges it above TOP 100,000.

sources.said: at the rate of 15% with effect from 1st April 2005
expects the total value of the taxable supplies of goods and/or services to be $100,000 or more in the next 12 months
